name: Compliance Monetisation & Ledger Gate Loop
description: A closed growth loop that intercepts free-tier operators at the BUSINESS_RESERVATION anchor boundary (5/month cap), surfaces a quantified KES revenue-exposure figure, and offers an immediate per-event M-Pesa escrow path at 2.5% of agreed fare as an alternative to subscription upgrade. Operators who repeatedly pay per-event fees receive inline copy showing cumulative cost vs Starter subscription price, driving subscription conversion. The loop self-reinforces: each QUOTA_EXCEEDED event that converts to a per-event escrow payment enriches the exposure ledger, which in turn sharpens the upgrade prompt shown on the next cycle. Redis-cached gate evaluation keeps the anchor-ledger endpoint within latency SLA while Daraja STK push callbacks atomically complete the escrow and fire the ledger anchor, ensuring >95% escrow reliability.
linked_feature: M-Pesa Payment Store & STK Push Flow

functions.name: getLedgerGateStatus
functions.signature: getLedgerGateStatus(orgId: string, billingPeriod: string, supabase: SupabaseClient, redis: Redis): Promise<LedgerGateStatus>
functions.logic: Accepts an orgId, a billingPeriod string (YYYY-MM), a Supabase client, and a Redis client. First attempts to read a cached LedgerGateStatus object from Redis using the key 'ledger_gate:{orgId}:{billingPeriod}'. On cache hit, parses and returns the cached value immediately. On cache miss, queries the ledger_anchor_usage view (or equivalent monthly count query on fleet_bookings) to obtain the current month's BUSINESS_RESERVATION anchor count for the org. Fetches the org's subscription tier from the organizations table to determine the applicable cap (free tier cap = 5). Constructs a LedgerGateStatus object with fields: { orgId, billingPeriod, currentCount, cap, isGated: currentCount >= cap, remainingSlots: Math.max(0, cap - currentCount), tier }. Serializes and stores this object in Redis with a 60-second TTL. Returns the LedgerGateStatus object. On any database error, logs the error and returns a safe default with isGated: false to avoid blocking legitimate paid-tier operators.

functions.name: assertLedgerNotGated
functions.signature: assertLedgerNotGated(orgId: string, bookingId: string, agreedFare: number, mpesaAccountLinked: boolean, supabase: SupabaseClient, redis: Redis): Promise<{ path: 'SUBSCRIPTION' | 'PER_EVENT'; gateStatus: LedgerGateStatus }>
functions.logic: Calls getLedgerGateStatus to obtain the current gate state. If isGated is false, returns { path: 'SUBSCRIPTION', gateStatus } immediately, allowing the standard subscription-path anchor to proceed. If isGated is true, evaluates whether a PER_EVENT path is available by checking that agreedFare > 0 and mpesaAccountLinked is true. If both conditions are met, returns { path: 'PER_EVENT', gateStatus } to signal the caller should initiate a per-event escrow. If the gate is closed and PER_EVENT conditions are not met (no fare or no M-Pesa account), throws a structured LedgerGateError with code 'QUOTA_EXCEEDED', the gateStatus object, and a human-readable message including the remaining slots and cap values. This error is intended to be caught by the API endpoint and serialized into a 402 response for the UI to render the QUOTA_EXCEEDED state.

functions.name: initiatePerEventEscrow
functions.signature: initiatePerEventEscrow(params: { orgId: string; bookingId: string; agreedFare: number; mpesaPhone: string; operatorName: string }, supabase: SupabaseClient, redis: Redis): Promise<{ checkoutRequestId: string; escrowRecordId: string; feeKes: number }>
functions.logic: Computes the escrow fee as Math.round(params.agreedFare * 0.025) in KES, with a minimum of 1 KES. Inserts a new row into per_event_escrow_records with status 'PENDING', the bookingId, orgId, agreedFare, escrowFeeKes, and a generated UUID as the record ID. Calls the M-Pesa provider's stkPush method with the computed fee amount, the operator's phone number, a description string referencing the booking ID, and an account reference. On STK push success, extracts the CheckoutRequestID from the Daraja response. Stores a Redis key 'per_event_escrow_intent:{CheckoutRequestID}' with a JSON payload containing { escrowRecordId, bookingId, orgId, feeKes } and a TTL of 3600 seconds (1 hour). Updates the per_event_escrow_records row with the CheckoutRequestID. Returns { checkoutRequestId, escrowRecordId, feeKes }. On STK push failure, updates the escrow record status to 'STK_FAILED' and throws an error with the Daraja error details. Invalidates the Redis ledger gate cache key for the org and current billing period after successful initiation to ensure the next gate check reflects the in-flight escrow.

functions.name: POST
functions.logic: Parses the Daraja STK push callback JSON body. Extracts Body.stkCallback.CheckoutRequestID and Body.stkCallback.ResultCode. Reads the Redis key 'per_event_escrow_intent:{CheckoutRequestID}' to retrieve { escrowRecordId, bookingId, orgId, feeKes }. If the Redis key is missing (expired or unknown), logs a warning and returns a 200 OK to Daraja (to prevent retries) with an error flag in the response body. If ResultCode === 0 (payment successful): calls anchorBusinessReservation with the bookingId and orgId to complete the ledger anchor; updates per_event_escrow_records row to status 'COMPLETED' with a completed_at timestamp and the MpesaReceiptNumber extracted from CallbackMetadata; updates the fleet_bookings row to set anchor_status = 'ANCHORED' and anchored_at timestamp; deletes the Redis intent key. If ResultCode !== 0 (payment failed): updates per_event_escrow_records status to 'PAYMENT_FAILED' with the ResultDesc; does not call anchorBusinessReservation; deletes the Redis intent key. In all cases, returns a 200 OK JSON response with { ResultCode: 0, ResultDesc: 'Accepted' } to satisfy Daraja's callback acknowledgement requirement. Wraps the entire handler in a try-catch; on unexpected errors, logs the error with the CheckoutRequestID for tracing and still returns 200 to Daraja.

functions.name: deriveInitialState
functions.logic: Pure function that maps a LedgerGateStatus object to the initial AnchorButtonState enum value for the component. If gateStatus is null or undefined, returns 'IDLE'. If gateStatus.isGated is false, returns 'IDLE' (operator has remaining quota). If gateStatus.isGated is true and the booking has an agreedFare > 0 and the org has mpesaAccountLinked, returns 'PER_EVENT_OFFER' to immediately surface the escrow path. If gateStatus.isGated is true but PER_EVENT conditions are not met, returns 'QUOTA_EXCEEDED' to surface the upgrade prompt. This function is called once on component mount and whenever the gateStatus prop changes, ensuring the button reflects the server-computed gate state without an additional round-trip.

integrations.description: Upstash Redis: used for two distinct caching purposes — (1) LedgerGateStatus cache with 60-second TTL keyed by org and billing period, and (2) per-event escrow intent store keyed by CheckoutRequestID with 1-hour TTL to correlate Daraja callbacks.

integrations.description: POST /api/fleet/bookings/[id]/anchor-ledger: the central routing endpoint that evaluates gate status, routes between SUBSCRIPTION and PER_EVENT paths, and returns structured responses for the LedgerAnchorButton UI state machine.

POST /api/mpesa/callbacks/per-event-escrow: public Daraja callback endpoint (no auth, validated by CheckoutRequestID lookup in Redis). Must return 200 with ResultCode 0 body to prevent Daraja retries.

LedgerAnchorButton.svelte: six-state button component embedded in the fleet booking detail view. Receives gateStatus as a server-side prop, manages local state transitions, and emits PostHog events on each transition. The QUOTA_EXCEEDED state renders operator-specific KES exposure and a subscription upgrade CTA.

telemetry.description: Fires when a per-event escrow record transitions to COMPLETED status — meaning the M-Pesa payment succeeded and anchorBusinessReservation was called. This is the single most meaningful growth signal in the loop: it confirms an operator who hit the quota gate chose the escrow path and successfully paid, making them a candidate for subscription conversion messaging.
